facts.claim: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Haiku 5.5, and Claude Mythos Preview have a 1M-token context window; for every such model, 1M is the default and no beta header is needed.
Other Claude models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5 (deprecated), have a 200k-token context window.
A single request to any of the 1M-context models can generate up to 128k output tokens (`max_tokens`).
A single request can include up to 600 images or PDF pages (100 for models with a 200k-token context window).

Everything in the request counts toward the context window: the system prompt, every message in `messages` (including tool results, images, and documents), and your tool definitions; the output Claude generates for the turn, including its extended thinking, counts too.
facts.value: system prompt + messages (incl. tool results) + tool definitions + output

facts.claim: If the input alone already exceeds the model's context window, the API returns a 400 `invalid_request_error` ("prompt is too long"); on Claude 4.5 models and newer, if generation reaches the context window limit it stops with `stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded"`.

Context editing is in beta; enable it with the beta header `context-management-2025-06-27`. Strategies: `clear_tool_uses_20250919` (tool result clearing) and `clear_thinking_20251015` (thinking block clearing).
Tool result clearing `trigger` defaults to 100,000 input tokens: once the prompt exceeds this threshold, clearing begins.
Tool result clearing `keep` defaults to 3 tool uses: how many recent tool use/result pairs to keep after clearing occurs.
Context editing is applied server-side before the prompt reaches Claude; your client application maintains the full, unmodified conversation history.

Compaction replaces the older turns of a conversation with a summary that Claude writes on the server; Compaction on demand uses the beta header `compact-2026-09-04` and the top-level `compaction` parameter, and Compaction at a token threshold triggers when input tokens reach the trigger you set.
Client-side compaction (SDK) `context_token_threshold` defaults to 100,000: the token count at which compaction triggers.
Claude Code auto memory: the first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context.

question.prompt: Support leads report that your agent "forgets" a customer's account tier mid-conversation in 11% of sessions, then applies the wrong refund policy. The tier comes from a get_customer call in turn 2. Context editing is enabled with tool result clearing at its default settings. Logs confirm the client sends the full, unmodified history on every request. Failures occur only in sessions whose input passes 100,000 tokens, all of which make more than three tool calls after turn 2. In a test cohort with context editing disabled, sessions above 100,000 tokens never lost the tier. What is the most likely root cause?

options.text: The model's recall of early turns weakens as conversations lengthen, which a more capable model with stronger long-context recall would fix.
Tool result clearing removed the turn-2 get_customer result once input passed its trigger, and nothing carried the tier outside clearable results.
The client is thinning early turns from the history to save tokens, so the turn-2 lookup is missing from the requests it sends to the API.
The tier sits in the middle of a long context and is overlooked through the lost in the middle effect once enough turns have accumulated.

autopsy.tempting: "Forgets" invites a model-capability explanation.
autopsy.ruledOutBy: The test cohort with context editing disabled never lost the tier above 100,000 tokens, so length alone does not degrade recall here.

autopsy.tempting: Thinning history is a classic cause of lost context.
autopsy.ruledOutBy: Logs confirm the client sends the full, unmodified history; context editing happens server-side.

autopsy.tempting: Position effects are a real cause of missed details.
autopsy.ruledOutBy: Turn 2 is near the beginning, and the cohort with context editing disabled kept the tier at the same lengths, so position is not the cause.

gate6.quantityInStem: The 100,000-token onset matches the default trigger (f8), and more than three later tool calls exceed the default keep of 3 (f9); both quantities are in the stem.
gate6.everyConstraintWorks: Full-history logs kill client thinning; the context-editing-disabled cohort kills recall decay and lost in the middle; the 100,000 onset and more-than-three later calls tie the failure to clearing defaults.
